geometry_edits.rationale: Open the notch to the west access side to create a legible public entry response.
Increase notch width to make the access carve spatially usable.
Extend the notch downward so the public threshold reaches the ground condition.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the public threshold by turning the existing minor notch into a clearer access-facing carve toward the verified road edge.
Align the notch to the program-frame access side so the ground response opens toward the street edge.
Widen the threshold carve enough to read as public entry rather than a decorative nick.
Lower the notch proportion so the carve engages the ground and lower-middle mass instead of only clipping the roofline.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent early mass in all four views, but it reads mostly as a compact stepped box with a bent roof cap rather than a neighborhood living figure. The parcel is respected in plan, yet the dominant gesture does not convincingly organize a public void or a legible street-facing threshold. The blue access edge appears adjacent to the mass, but the ground response is weak and semantically muted; there is no clear court, notch, or undercut opening toward access. The silhouette is not bad as an object, but the section and void logic do not yet support the program brief for active ground, one clear public space, and calm upper hierarchy. It resembles a generic stacked pavilion more than a mixed-use neighborhood building, so program_fit_hard_pass fails.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more clearly a cultural pavilion than residential mixed-use; transfer the courtyard-and-bridge logic, not the typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise composition with a large central void and a modest bridge/connection can support neighborhood publicness without becoming tower-like.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger and more complex than the candidate; avoid copying the perimeter tower/campus scale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like clustering around a central public landscape can produce a legible neighborhood figure with strong open-space hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate lacks the open perimeter/transparent ground logic seen here.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A long horizontal mass with a central void and responsive roof can read as active mixed-use ground with calm upper continuity.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is more sectional and landscape-integrated; the candidate is currently too compact and boxy.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, ribbon-like massing with bridging and layered circulation can create a coherent neighborhood section.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate has some massing hierarchy but not the same level of interlock or courtyard legibility.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes around a central courtyard, with voids under elevated blocks, can support an active public threshold.

warnings: Access-edge response is underdeveloped despite the visible frontage.
Open-space figure is too shallow to count as a meaningful public court.
Upper stepping is coherent but not yet program-meaningful enough to rescue the weak ground condition.
